Specifically we need:

- Retention tiers and whether on-demand retrieval beyond retention window is supported (and how)
- Any PII redaction/field-level masking you apply before handing material to customers
- Expected time to deliver a historical snapshot and typical file sizes / cost drivers

We also saw mention of a "signed snapshot" in your docs — can you confirm what the signature covers and whether it includes a content hash for non-repudiation?

Could you provide a short runbook we can include in our SIG evidence package? If helpful, we can schedule a quick call.

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. I've drafted a short runbook below (high level) and looped in Marissa and Neha for details on retention and export mechanics. Quick answers up front: we support both a self-serve time-windowed query API for on-demand slices and an orchestrated export (S3 pre-signed URL) for complete snapshots. Signed snapshots include a SHA-256 manifest and a signed envelope from our KMS key for chain-of-custody.

Runbook (summary):
1) Request type decision
   - Quick slice (<=24 hours, small volume): use Query API endpoint /v1/audit/logs/query with start/end timestamps and a tenant_id. Returns ndjson stream, paginated.
   - Full snapshot (multi-day / compliance evidence): create a Snapshot Job via POST /v1/audit/snapshots with window, filters, and delivery target.

2) Data components included
   - Event envelope (timestamp, event_type, tenant_id, actor_id, resource_id) — always included
   - Full payload (request/response): optional flag; included in snapshots when requested and where policy permits
   - System metadata (node id, processing latency) included for root-cause investigations

3) Delivery and integrity
   - Snapshot build produces gzipped ndjson files in customer-owned or Redwood-managed S3 bucket. Delivery options: pre-signed S3 URL (short-lived) or direct push to customer S3 with cross-account role.
   - Manifest.json contains per-file SHA-256 + snapshot-level signature (KMS RSA-PSS). Manifest is time-stamped and stored with snapshot.

4) Redaction and PII handling
   - Default: raw snapshot includes payloads marked as non-sensitive. Fields flagged by our PII classifier are redacted by default for hosted tenants; enterprise/contracted customers can request unredacted exports with audited controls and additional DPA addendum.

5) Turnaround and SLAs
   - Query API: immediate (subject to quota); slices are streamed and costed by token/event count.
   - Snapshot jobs: typical build time for 7-day windows ~ 2–6 hours depending on volume; large multi-week windows can take 12+ hours. We offer expedited job priority for an uplift.

6) Costs and limits
   - Pricing: snapshot jobs charged by scanned events + storage egress when delivering to external bucket. Real-world estimates vary; sample cost matrix included in attached runbook.

Please see attached runbook (v1.2) for step-by-step commands, sample curl requests, and RBAC requirements. Marissa, can you confirm our retention tiers and whether we can execute an export older than retention (i.e., cold-archive retrieval)?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you'd like to walk through an example window.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee

Thanks for the summary, Soojin — adding retention details and implementation notes.

Retention tiers (hosted customers):
- Hot (30 days): immediate query API and snapshot builds are fast (metadata + payload).
- Warm (31–365 days): data is kept accessible in S3 warm tier; snapshot job will include a read-step that may add 1–3 hours depending on window size.
- Cold (>1 year): archived to Glacier-like tier; retrieval requires restore operation and costs/time (typically 24–72 hours to restore prior to snapshot build) and will be treated as "archival retrieval" with separate approval.

Export mechanics notes:
- For self-serve Query API we limit max window to 14 days and a max page size to avoid resource contention; larger windows must use Snapshot Jobs.
- Snapshot Jobs are executed by the audit pipeline with job-level isolation; jobs produce a manifest signed with our KMS signing key; we also optionally include a per-event hash chain (Merkle root) on request for higher integrity guarantees.
- Redaction: we support field-level redaction rules that can be applied at export time. Customers requesting unredacted payloads must have an approved DPA addendum and an OLA for handling sensitive fields.

Karthik — from an engineering perspective, note that we can expose a temporary read-only Query API key to customers that want programmatic slices; keys are rate-limited and logged, and all query activity appears in the tenant's audit trail (so customers get visibility into who requested what).

I'll also confirm cost buckets in the attached spreadsheet (in the runbook).

– Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Security & Compliance

Hi Alice — following up with two small clarifications and an offer for a quick walkthrough:

1) Signed snapshot scope: The signature covers the manifest.json (file list + per-file SHA-256), snapshot start/end timestamps, and the snapshot job id. The manifest is time-stamped and notarized by our KMS; we maintain an immutable log of manifest signatures for 7 years for enterprise contracts. If you need per-event digital signatures we can enable a Merkle proof option (adds build time).

2) Redaction workflow: default hosted behavior redacts fields flagged by our classifier. If you'd like unredacted exports we can support that under an addendum; this will be delivered to a customer-managed bucket only and requires a security attestation form.

Next steps:
- I can schedule a 30-minute runbook walkthrough with your SecOps team to run a demo snapshot for a 7-day window and show the manifest verification steps. Proposed times: Nov 3 or Nov 4, mornings PST.
- I'll attach the runbook v1.2 and the signed-query-schema.json (already attached above).

If that works, tell me which slot you prefer and we'll send a calendar invite + temporary test credentials (read-only).
